question: Assume today is 2026-08-17. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the seasonally adjusted annual rate of privately-owned housing starts in the United States in August 2026 (the number of housing units at an annual rate, as in '1,300,000'), as it will be first reported in the U.S. Census Bureau and HUD Monthly New Residential Construction release.

target.what: Seasonally adjusted annual rate of privately-owned housing starts (new privately-owned housing units started) in the United States, as first reported by the U.S. Census Bureau and HUD in the Monthly New Residential Construction release for August 2026
target.publisher: U.S. Census Bureau and U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), Monthly New Residential Construction (joint release)
target.caveats: Target period (August 2026) is future/ongoing relative to the 2026-08-17 cutoff; the August release would normally publish in mid-to-late September 2026, after the cutoff, so no August print exists at cutoff. Working interpretation: privately-owned housing starts only (excludes publicly-owned starts

candidates.hypothesis: Recent monthly SAAR prints (through July 2026, published before cutoff) plus seasonal factors and month-to-month momentum anchor a short-horizon forecast of the August 2026 SAAR; August typically shows a modest seasonal-adjustment-neutral pattern relative to July.
candidates.data_to_find: Privately-owned housing starts SAAR for each month from roughly 2024 through July 2026 (latest available before cutoff), plus the not-seasonally-adjusted August counts and seasonal factors for prior years to gauge typical July-to-August SAAR change.
search_hints: Census Bureau new residential construction housing starts July 2026
privately owned housing starts SAAR monthly 2025 2026
housing starts historical table seasonally adjusted annual rate

candidates.hypothesis: Building permits (especially single-family authorizations) lead starts by roughly one to two months; the July 2026 permit SAAR and single-family permit trend constrain the August starts level, since starts cannot persistently exceed authorized pipeline.
candidates.data_to_find: Building permits SAAR and single-family permits SAAR for June and July 2026 (published before cutoff), plus the historical permits-to-starts ratio and lag structure.

candidates.perspective: Census housing completions and under-construction stock
candidates.hypothesis: Units under construction and completions reflect the pipeline; a large under-construction backlog supports continued starts, while a shrinking backlog signals deceleration. Completions and under-construction stock bracket plausible starts.
candidates.data_to_find: Housing units under construction and housing completions SAAR for mid-2026, plus historical relationship between under-construction stock and starts.

candidates.perspective: NAHB / builder sentiment and single-family market
candidates.hypothesis: NAHB/Wells Fargo Housing Market Index and single-family starts move together; a mid-2026 HMI reading and mortgage-rate environment indicate whether single-family starts are trending up or down into August.
candidates.data_to_find: NAHB Housing Market Index for July/August 2026 (if published before cutoff), 30-year mortgage rate trend mid-2026, and historical HMI-to-single-family-starts relationship.

candidates.hypothesis: Published forecasts or nowcasts of August 2026 housing starts (e.g., from banks, Fannie Mae, MBA, or consensus panels) made before cutoff provide a direct anchor, though they may share underlying data sources.
candidates.data_to_find: Any pre-cutoff forecast or nowcast for August 2026 (or Q3 2026) housing starts SAAR, with the forecast date and source; note whether it is a point estimate or range.

candidates.hypothesis: Starts are the sum of regional activity; Census regional (Northeast, Midwest, South, West) starts data through July 2026 and any state-level permit surges (e.g., South multifamily) can be aggregated and trended to August.
candidates.data_to_find: Census regional housing starts SAAR for recent months through July 2026, and any notable state-level permit or starts anomalies in mid-2026.

candidates.hypothesis: Mortgage rates, labor market, tariffs on building materials, and any mid-2026 policy or weather shocks shift the August starts level relative to trend; measurable exposure (rate changes, material cost indices) adjusts the baseline.
candidates.data_to_find: 30-year mortgage rate path June-August 2026, lumber/material price indices mid-2026, and any documented weather or policy disruptions affecting construction in August 2026.

candidates.hypothesis: The SAAR is the NSA monthly count times a seasonal factor times 12; knowing the typical August seasonal factor and the NSA August level relative to July lets us convert a July NSA base into an August SAAR estimate.
candidates.data_to_find: Census X-13 seasonal factors for housing starts by month (recent vintage), and NSA monthly starts for July and prior Augusts to estimate the typical seasonal factor and month-over-month NSA pattern.

methods.label: m1

p1.role: June 2026 privately-owned total housing starts SAAR, base for August 2026 forecast

methods.rationale: Anchors on the most recent total starts print (June 2026, 1,427k) and applies a reversion factor reflecting the multifamily-driven spike and softening permits. Shared dependency: relies on June being a valid base; failure mode is that the June spike fully persists or fully reverses.

methods.label: m2

p10.role: June 2026 single-family starts SAAR, base for August 2026

p46.role: June 2026 5+ unit starts SAAR, base for August 2026

methods.rationale: Decomposes total starts into single-family (stable, 895k) and 5+ unit (volatile, 513k) components, each trended to August with separate ratios. This captures the different dynamics of the two segments. Failure mode: 2-4 unit starts are omitted (small residual), and the multifamily ratio is highly uncertain.

excluded_by_input_audit.label: m3
excluded_by_input_audit.reason: input audit: p3: Building permits are a different quantity (authorized units) than housing starts; using permits as a proxy for starts is not the target quantity, and the role itself mislabels the evidence as a st; a1: The assumption is a starts-to-starts reversion ratio (August-to-June total starts ratio), not a starts-to-permit ratio as the role requires; it does not bridge permits to starts.

kept.name: August-to-June total starts ratio (reversion factor)
kept.rationale: June 2026 total starts (1,427k) were a multifamily-driven spike well above May (1,199k); permits (1,367k) and rising mortgage rates suggest partial reversion by August. A ratio near 0.9 reflects typical mean reversion of a spike month toward the permit-implied level, with wide range for monthly nois
kept.applies_when: June 2026 is a representative base and August reverts partway toward the permit-implied trend.
kept.falsified_by: A July 2026 starts print near or above 1,427k, or a July permit surge, would indicate no reversion.

kept.name: August-to-June single-family starts ratio
kept.rationale: Single-family starts were flat May-to-June (897k to 895k) and single-family permits softened modestly (892k to 871k); rising mortgage rates (6.48% to 6.66%) and material costs are mild headwinds, so a near-flat ratio with modest downside is appropriate.
kept.applies_when: Single-family starts continue their stable trend into August.
kept.falsified_by: A sharp single-family permit drop or mortgage-rate spike above ~7% would push the ratio lower.

kept.name: August-to-June multifamily (5+ unit) starts ratio
kept.rationale: June 5+ unit starts (513k) were unusually high and multifamily is the most volatile component; permits for 5+ units (445k) sit well below the June starts rate, implying a pullback. A ratio below 1 with a wide range reflects this volatility.
kept.applies_when: Multifamily starts revert toward the lower permit-implied pace.
kept.falsified_by: A July 5+ unit permit surge or a large multifamily starts print would overturn the reversion assumption.

residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
